speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin our evaluation of your systemic hypertension, how old are you and have you noticed any headaches, vision changes, or swelling in your legs?

speaker: Patient
text: 5-year-old boy. The patient is presented by his mother for a well-child visit. The boy was born at 39 weeks gestation via spontaneous vaginal delivery, is currently up to date on all vaccines, and is meeting all developmental milestones. His mother reports that he has been generally doing well with no concerns. No family history of cardiovascular disease. The boy does not take any medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Since he is a 5-year-old with systemic hypertension, we need to determine if this is primary or secondary in origin. Have you noticed any episodes of severe flank pain, abdominal pain, or unexplained blood in his urine?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is High blood pressure on the right upper extremity. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Migraine and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is an unusual description; a 5-year-old with isolated right upper extremity hypertension strongly suggests coarctation of the aorta, especially with no mention of lower extremity pulses or blood pressure. Please ensure the child has a lower extremity blood pressure measurement taken immediately, as the discrepancy between upper and lower limbs is our most critical finding. REQUEST TEST: Upper and Lower Extremity Blood Pressure, EKG, Abdominal Ultrasound. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray, Echocardiogram.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Blood_Pressure_Right_Upper_Extremity: 150/80 mm Hg; Blood_Pressure_Differential: Upper_Extremities 150/80 mm Hg (Right), Compared to lower values in lower extremities; Echocardiogram Findings: Narrowing of the aorta distal to the left subclavian artery with a gradient, consistent with coarctation. Left ventricular function is normal.; Chest_X-ray Findings: Normal heart size, rib notching not observed (may not be present in young children); Pulses: 2+ radial pulses and trace femoral pulses; Heart_Auscultation: Normal S1 and S2, 2/6 long systolic murmur with systolic ejection click over the left sternal border and back.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Coarctation of the Aorta. The confirmed blood pressure differential, trace femoral pulses, and echocardiogram findings of aortic narrowing distal to the left subclavian artery are diagnostic. We will need to schedule an angiography or CT angiogram to define the anatomy prior to surgical repair.
